correctness.rationale: For any nonadjacent rook cells the only two length-two geodesics pass through the two opposing rectangle corners. Hence full selected rectangles are exactly the visibility obstructions. The induced graph is the line graph of the chosen row-column incidence graph; selected cells are connected iff the chosen incidence edges share one component. Each row pair can occur in at most one multirow column, leaving exactly five mutually exclusive cases. Casewise necessary/sufficient connectivity and binomial generating factors prove all coefficients for all n>=3. Maximal degree and multiplicity follow from a strict comparison among family maxima. Exhaustive independent vertex-set enumeration for 1<=n<=5 (n>=3 being the theorem domain) confirms every coefficient but is not an infinite proof.

The five-class structural derivation adds a nontrivial induced-connectivity restriction and gives a genuinely new explicit count throughout an infinite natural family; no stronger published/result-record claim was found in actual targeted searches. value.rationale: The natural rank-three Hamming graph K3 square Kn is an archetypal rook graph whose ordinary mutual visibility encodes forbidden rectangles. Connected mutual visibility was introduced only in 2026, and determining the full size distribution of connected feasible sets is a motivated strengthening of its maximum-parameter problem, not a toy isolated case. The finite-state row-pair rigidity gives an exact five-class theorem uniform in n, a full nonempty cardinality polynomial, and exact labeled extremal multiplicities; these are not a restatement of the older C4-free existence criterion. Value does not rely on any claim of independent validation.
